elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “Customer, its Affiliates.”

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”
The clause does not state that paid-up licences are perpetual, and it is not demonstrably established that paid-up licences cannot arise.

Although at-will revocability was removed, the clause does not make paid-up licences irrevocable and permits termination upon expiration or termination of the Agreement or applicable Service Option Attachment.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: IBM may terminate upon any expiration or termination of the Agreement or applicable Service Option Attachment, without limiting the underlying termination event to material breach.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no uncured-breach condition or cure requirement.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: No transfer or successor right is included.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates are covered upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause covers Customer's Affiliates automatically, without requiring notice or consent, which provides broader affiliate coverage than coverage activated by written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no transfer right for an M&A successor.

result.reason: The redline appropriately removes at-will revocability and adds Affiliates and contractors, but it reaches neither complete position. It omits all successor-transfer rights, does not protect paid-up licences as perpetual and irrevocable, and allows subscription licence termination based on any expiration or termination of the governing agreement rather than only an uncured material breach. The Services-use limitation and software restrictions remain intact, so unrelated commercial intent is preserved.
